diagnostics.message: data.google_dns_keys.dns_keys reads managed_zone = local.managed_zone.id, which resolves to google_dns_managed_zone.dns_managed_zone[0] when var.zone_config is set, but no dependency on that resource is recorded. On a fresh apply the data source can be read before the zone is created / DNSSEC keys exist (404 from the DNS API). It must depend on the managed-zone resource.

resource.google_dns_managed_zone_iam_binding.iam_bindings sets managed_zone = local.managed_zone.id, which resolves to google_dns_managed_zone.dns_managed_zone[0] when var.zone_config is set, but no dependency on that resource is recorded. IAM bindings could be applied against a zone that does not exist yet in the same run (404). It must depend on the managed-zone resource (bare depends_on; the local-based reference cannot be inlined cleanly without duplicating the resource/data branching).

The explicit depends_on of resource.google_dns_record_set.dns_record_set on resource.google_dns_managed_zone.dns_managed_zone is redundant: each record set's name attribute (each.value.resource_name from local.recordsets) already interpolates local.managed_zone.dns_name, which references google_dns_managed_zone.dns_managed_zone[0], so Terraform already orders record sets after zone creation via an attribute reference.
